scope.question: What is the smallest factory-as-code runtime that can execute engineering now and later execute research/writing and GTM without making “agent” or “chat” the unit of truth?
in_scope: A shared execution kernel; repository-owned domain packs; artifact, event, gate, identity, capability, evaluation and handoff contracts; failure/recovery; engineering-first extraction gates; separately configured GTM repository.
out_of_scope: A universal ontology, dynamic plugin marketplace, general autonomous business operator, cross-domain shared secrets, LLM-controlled authorization, unreviewed publication/outreach/CRM mutation, or recursive self-modification.
scope.decision: Build an artifact factory, not an agent platform. The minimum shared nouns are FactoryDefinition, Run, Step, Artifact, Event, Gate, CapabilityGrant, Receipt and Evaluation. A worker (human, model, deterministic program or external service) is an interchangeable executor referenced by a step, not the state owner. Conversation is typed artifacts and events, not hidden chat state. Ship only the engineering domain pack first. Keep research as a proving fixture/read-only workflow. Start a separate GTM repository and domain pack only after explicit extraction and value gates.

verified_capabilities.claim: Durable workflow engines can preserve history and retry activities, but deterministic replay constrains workflow code and does not make effects exactly once.
verified_capabilities.evidence: Temporal documents event history/replay, activity retry and idempotency guidance [S3,S4].

verified_capabilities.claim: Existing pipeline systems already demonstrate typed DAG composition without an agent/chat abstraction.
verified_capabilities.evidence: Tekton defines Tasks/Pipelines/Results/Workspaces; Argo defines DAG/steps, templates, artifacts and lifecycle hooks [S5,S6].

verified_capabilities.claim: Interoperable event and provenance envelopes exist.
verified_capabilities.evidence: CloudEvents specifies common context attributes; W3C PROV models entities/activities/agents; in-toto/SLSA attestations bind subjects, predicates and builders [S7-S10].

verified_capabilities.claim: GitHub supports reusable workflows, OIDC, environments, rulesets and artifact attestations, but those are remote mutable controls and not a complete cross-domain state store.
verified_capabilities.evidence: Official GitHub docs [S11-S15]; prior validated repository studies found a durable ledger/reconciler is still needed.

verified_capabilities.claim: GTM products expose real workflows around CRM records, journeys, experiments, approvals and content, not merely “marketing agents.”
verified_capabilities.evidence: Salesforce consent/data docs, HubSpot email approvals, Braze Canvas experiments/control groups and Adobe GenStudio approvals document bounded operational surfaces [S20-S24].

verified_capabilities.claim: Regulation creates deterministic publication and outreach boundaries.
verified_capabilities.evidence: GDPR principles/lawful basis and data-subject rights, FTC CAN-SPAM obligations, and NIST privacy/AI risk guidance require purpose, minimization, identity, opt-out/suppression and accountable review [S25-S29].

supported: A domain-neutral durable kernel is supported by workflow and event/provenance standards.
Repository-owned schemas plus typed artifacts can represent engineering PRs, research evidence records and GTM briefs/campaign variants without treating them as messages.
Hard gates and scoped identities are mature infrastructure patterns.

Kubernetes/SPIFFE/OCI/NIST guidance supports layered workload identity, tenancy and digest-bound cross-repository trust, while explicitly showing that a namespace or registry alone is not a security boundary [S39-S43].
not_supported: No audited evidence establishes one universal cross-domain ontology or unattended GTM factory.
Vendor feature pages establish availability, not uplift, compliance, brand safety or correctness.
A durable workflow provides at-least-once execution semantics around effects unless application-level idempotency/receipts reconcile ambiguity.
Provenance proves who/what produced bytes, not truth, legal permission, brand fitness or business value.

SaaS privacy/approval switches are configuration- and SKU-dependent; Super Admin or API/transactional paths can bypass some UI gates [S21,S44,S53-S59]. The factory’s own capability proxy must enforce final effects.
independent_challenges: METR found experienced open-source developers 19% slower in its early-2025 randomized setting [S30], so engineering agent capability is not an automatic ROI premise.
MAST catalogued recurring multi-agent coordination failures [S31]; therefore fanout is a controlled composition feature, not the architecture.
Noy and Zhang found faster writing in bounded professional tasks [S32], but that does not validate publication, factuality or GTM outcomes.
The Answer.AI Devin trial reported 3 successes in 20 tasks [S33], challenging broad vendor autonomy claims.

Field evidence is heterogeneous: support-agent gains [S51] and consultant gains inside the model frontier but lower correctness outside it [S52] support task-specific evaluation and hard stop boundaries, not global GTM autonomy.
missing_denominators: No local baselines yet for engineering acceptance, escaped defects, reviewer time, cost and cycle time.
No GTM baseline yet for consent defects, approval latency, brand edits, deliverability, qualified pipeline, incrementality or opt-out/complaint rates.
No evidence yet that two domains truly require identical extension APIs rather than a copied small kernel.

shared_runtime_actors: scheduler: evaluates dependencies, budgets and quotas
human gate service: records authenticated exact-version decisions
trust_rules: Each run has tenant/project/repository/domain identity. No ambient cross-repo token.
Executors receive short-lived capability grants for exact resource/action/scope/budget/expiry/fence.
Proposer cannot approve its own output, evaluator, policy, grant or promotion.
GTM model workers cannot send, publish, change suppression/consent, merge identities, overwrite CRM system-of-record fields, or change attribution definitions. They draft or propose only.
Cross-repo handoff is accepted by the receiving controller after schema, provenance, policy and owner checks; the sender has no write authority in the receiver.

Use project × environment as the tenancy key. Namespace/row/bucket prefixes alone are not a hard boundary: separate workload identity, encryption key, quota and default-deny network policy; use separate clusters/control planes for hostile or regulated tenants [S39-S43].

complete_state_catalog.terminal_rule: SUCCEEDED is terminal only for an exact definition/input/policy digest. New input or invalidated approval creates a new run/revision; it never rewrites history.

transition_contract.event_envelope: CloudEvents-like immutable event: id, source, specversion, type, subject, time, tenant_id, project_id, repository_id, domain, run_id, step_id, attempt, sequence, causation_id, correlation_id, definition_digest, policy_digest, data_digest and traceparent.
transition_contract.command_rule: A command carries expected_state_version and idempotency_key. The controller transaction validates actor/grant, state/guard, dependency versions, quotas and budgets; appends event plus outbox record; then returns the new version. Duplicate keys return the prior receipt.
transition_contract.effect_rule: Effects use prepare/execute/record/reconcile. Receipt keys are tenant/run/step/effect-kind/target/logical-key. Timeouts are UNKNOWN, not failed; read observed state before retry. Destructive/non-idempotent effects require a human gate or adapter-specific dedupe token.
invalidation: Input/spec/definition/policy/output digest changes invalidate dependent approvals/evaluations.
Lease expiry increments a fencing token; stale workers cannot commit checkpoints/effects.
Consent/suppression/brand-policy or audience-query changes invalidate GTM send/publish approval.
Base SHA or acceptance oracle changes invalidate engineering verification/merge approval.
Rendered content, target query/count, schedule/channel, consent/suppression snapshot, substantiation or brand/policy revision invalidates the corresponding GTM approval [S44-S47].
transition_contract.reconciliation: Webhooks accelerate observation; periodic full scans repair missed/reordered events. External systems are projections or systems of record named per field. Conflicts pause and surface ownership; never last-write-wins silently.
transition_contract.cancellation_rollback: Cancellation stops new leases, requests cooperative stop, revokes grants, reconciles in-flight effects, runs only predeclared compensations, verifies cleanup and ends CANCELLED or ROLLED_BACK; failed compensation escalates.

principles: Artifacts are immutable content-addressed facts; mutable systems are referenced through observations and receipts.
A domain pack owns kind schemas, semantic validators and redaction/retention rules. The kernel only understands the envelope.
Inputs are pinned by digest. Outputs declare which inputs and tool/model/data versions produced them.
External URLs are evidence only with retrieval metadata and, where allowed, captured digest/snapshot.
artifact_contracts.gtm_specific: Never export raw contact data in a generic artifact. Store a scoped query/reference, field-level classification, lawful-basis/purpose, consent/suppression snapshot/version, residency/retention, approved channel, frequency cap and subject-count. Separate content approval from audience/send approval. Audience exports are sensitive artifacts: keep raw lists outside ordinary artifact storage and model context. Record query AST, expected/actual count and redacted QA. Brand, legal/privacy, deliverability and business approvals are separate decisions, not one boolean.

conversation_and_handoffs.conversation_model: Chat is an optional view. Durable semantic records are Question, Answer, Decision, Assumption, Dissent, Approval, Checkpoint and Summary artifacts. Every record has author, timestamp, scope, supersedes, evidence links and affected digests. Free text is untrusted input until promoted into a typed record.
conversation_and_handoffs.resume: A worker resumes from the latest verified checkpoint plus unresolved questions/decisions and pinned artifact manifest, never from a transcript alone. Compaction emits a signed summary with covered event range; original events remain auditable.
conversation_and_handoffs.cross_repo_handoff: Sender emits a HandoffManifest containing schema URI/version, producer repo+commit, artifact digests, provenance/attestations, allowed purpose, data classification, retention, owner, expiry, expected consumer/domain and requested action. Receiver imports by reference/copy into quarantine, validates compatibility/policy, obtains local approval, records ACCEPTED/REJECTED and maps to a new local work item. No shared mutable work item or transitive token.
examples: Engineering release evidence -> GTM release-note brief: public API/change facts only; GTM cannot read source secrets or trigger deploy.
Research claim ledger -> engineering spec or GTM positioning: claims retain citations/confidence; receiving owner approves interpretation.
GTM feedback aggregate -> engineering issue: de-identified segment/count/evidence; no raw CRM contacts; product owner re-prioritizes locally.
conversation_and_handoffs.compatibility: Support current and previous major handoff schemas during a measured migration window; reject unknown required fields/major versions; transformations are versioned, tested artifacts with loss reports.

constraints: No arbitrary runtime code in guards; evaluate a small total expression language over validated metadata.
Fanout declares maximum cardinality, concurrency, cost/token/time/egress budgets and cancellation behavior.
Subfactory interface is typed artifacts, not shared memory. Child cannot inherit capabilities unless explicitly narrowed.
Cleanup is a mandatory finally path and is itself reconciled.
Domain packs compose primitives and adapters; they do not inject controller code.
orchestration_and_composition.avoid_plugin_platform: For v1, ship a fixed adapter set: local/OCI command, GitHub, object store, Postgres, HTTP with allowlist, model inference and human approval. New adapters are ordinary reviewed runtime releases, not dynamically loaded repository plugins. Add a stable extension SDK only after two production domains expose the same missing interface at least three times and security/operations can support it.

deterministic_ask: Required typed field/decision is absent, contradictory or below configured confidence.
Multiple materially different interpretations alter acceptance, audience, claim, spend, legal basis or publication.
Requested capability is outside allowlist; budget/time/retry threshold would be exceeded.
Schema/provenance/digest validation fails; external state conflicts; compensation/reconciliation is ambiguous.

Any PII/sensitive data purpose change, new audience source, consent/suppression uncertainty, brand exception, public claim without evidence, regulated content, first use of channel/template/segment, send/publish, CRM merge/delete/system-of-record overwrite.
Engineering: product intent/architecture/security/data migration, protected policy/eval/CI/permissions changes, merge, deploy or rollback exceptions.
Any material advertising claim lacks current substantiation or the proposed effect changes sale/sharing/opt-out/GPC behavior [S48-S50].
human_need_policy.probabilistic_signal_rule: Model confidence can only tighten controls. If calibrated risk score >= domain threshold, disagreement among independent checks exceeds threshold, or evidence coverage falls below threshold, route to clarification/review. A high confidence score can never bypass a deterministic gate.
stop: Repeated same-class failure reaches retry cap
unexpected target cardinality or blast radius
human_need_policy.approval_contract: Named role approves an exact artifact/input/policy/definition digest, action, target set, budget, expiry and conditions. Any bound change invalidates it. Silence, chat assent, Project status or model judgement is not approval.

kernel_schema.inputs/outputs: named artifact kind + schema URI/version + classification
kernel_schema.steps: id, uses(adapter/executor profile), needs, consumes, produces, capability_profile, retry, timeout, budget, gate, compensation
kernel_schema.policies: risk class, retention, quotas, human roles, failure/stop
kernel_schema.triggers: disabled by default; authenticated event/schedule/manual plus admission gate

factory_as_code_schema.example:
apiVersion: factory.polar.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Factory
metadata:
  name: engineering-ticket-to-draft-pr
  domain: engineering
  owner: team-platform
  repository: product-api
spec:
  inputs:
    ticket: {kind: eng.polar.dev/ReadySpec@v1, classification: internal}
  outputs:
    proposal: {kind: eng.polar.dev/PatchEvidence@v1}
  trigger: {type: github.issue.ready, enabled: true, admissionGate: ready-v1}
  budgets: {wallTime: 2h, costUSD: 20, attempts: 2, fanout: 3}
  steps:
    - id: plan
      uses: executor/model
      consumes: [ticket]
      produces: [eng.polar.dev/Plan@v1]
      capabilities: [repo.read]
    - id: implement
      needs: [plan]
      uses: executor/oci-command
      capabilities: [repo.branch.write, ci.dispatch]
      produces: [eng.polar.dev/Patch@v1]
      retry: {max: 1, idempotency: required}
      compensation: cleanup-workspace
    - id: verify
      needs: [implement]
      uses: verifier/clean-room
      produces: [eng.polar.dev/PatchEvidence@v1]
    - id: draft-pr
      needs: [verify]
      gate: {policy: exact-digest-review, role: technical-owner}
      uses: github/create-draft-pr
      capabilities: [github.pr.create]
  evaluations:
    - {metric: acceptance_pass, threshold: 1.0, owner: independent-verifier}
factory_as_code_schema.gtm_repository_rule: A future `gtm-factory-config` repository defines `gtm.polar.dev/*` schemas and factories. Every trigger is `enabled:false` until privacy, brand, CRM steward and channel-owner gates are configured. Draft generation may enable first; audience materialization, CRM write, send and publish remain distinct gated steps. Runtime code is pinned as an image/digest and cannot be overridden by repository scripts.
factory_as_code_schema.schema_evolution: Additive minor changes; explicit converters for major versions; lock file pins runtime/adapters/domain-pack/schema digests; plan/apply/re-read upgrade; canary one repository; preserve unknown domain fields; rollback by prior immutable bundle.

engineering_first: Authenticated issue -> normalized ReadySpec -> human readiness token -> fenced lease -> isolated plan/patch -> exact-head independent verification -> draft PR -> CODEOWNER/merge gate -> merge/release/canary -> outcome/feedback -> reviewed eval candidate. This is the only production write workflow in phase 1.
research_writing_fixture: Question/fields -> approved scope -> bounded source acquisition -> parallel SourceRecords -> ClaimLedger join/dedup/conflict pass -> citation audit -> editor decision -> report/publication package. Web retrieval is untrusted; publication is gated. Initially run internally/read-only to test typed artifacts, fanout/join, resume and provenance without a second write domain.
gtm_later: Approved market question -> evidence-backed ICP/positioning -> campaign brief -> variants constrained by BrandRuleSet -> factual/legal/brand review -> audience query proposal -> privacy/consent/suppression and CRM steward gate -> experiment design with holdout/primary metric/stop rule -> channel payload -> separate send/publish approval -> channel receipt -> immutable metric snapshot -> attribution/incrementality analysis -> CRM change proposals -> reviewed learnings. Models never directly send/publish or mutate canonical consent/identity.
gtm_metrics: Operational: approval latency, edits per artifact, failure/retry, deliverability, bounce, unsubscribe, spam complaint, suppression violations. Experiment: predeclared primary metric, assignment unit, holdout, sample/exposure, confidence interval, guardrails. Business: qualified opportunities/pipeline/revenue with window and attribution definition. Brand: reviewer rubric/violation class. Privacy/compliance: unauthorized access, purpose/consent/retention defects. Report denominators and cost; do not optimize clicks alone.

Publication package must include substantiation per material claim, rendered preview, exact target snapshot, schedule/channel, brand/policy versions and separate approval digests. Provider/UI approval cannot be trusted as the only guard because supported API or transactional paths may bypass it [S44].
handoff_flow: receiver owner accepts and creates local run
optional aggregate feedback returns through a new handoff

automated_loop: Collect version-bound outcomes, costs, human edits, failures and policy denials.
Cluster candidate failures and draft postmortem/regression case.
Human curator validates ground truth/redaction and admits eval case.
Proposer creates minimal prompt/workflow/schema/adapter change in protected PR.
Independent runner performs replay, security/fault tests and reports subgroup regressions.
Run read-only shadow, then bounded canary on an allowlisted class.
Independent owner promotes exact digest or controller auto-rolls back on predeclared thresholds.
protected_invariants: Agents cannot alter identity/IAM, secret broker, capability profiles, approval roles, audit/event history, retention/legal holds, consent/suppression, trusted builders, policy engine, hidden/holdout evals, metric/attribution definitions, kill switches or promotion/rollback thresholds.
A candidate cannot grade or approve itself; training/eval data lineage and contamination checks remain independent.
Cross-domain evidence cannot silently change purpose/classification; new use requires receiving-domain approval.
Successful output is sampled; failures and cancellations stay in denominators.
self_improvement_boundary.promotion: Require exact artifact/runtime/domain-pack digests, predefined non-inferiority margins, security pass, cost/latency budget, subgroup analysis, minimum sample/window, no severe incident, two-role approval for protected components and automatic rollback handle.
self_improvement_boundary.rollback: Revoke bundle, stop admission, fence active attempts where required, restore prior pinned bundle, reconcile effects, preserve evidence and open incident/postmortem. Never delete unfavorable evals.
self_improvement_boundary.why_not_recursive: Prompt injection remains unresolved [S34]; provenance is not correctness; metrics can be gamed; and evaluators share correlated model failure. Therefore the improvement loop may propose and test, but independent governance owns ground truth and promotion.

schema_contract: JSON Schema/CUE validation; golden domain fixtures; unknown-major rejection; converter round trips; content digest/media/classification tests.
transition_property: Model-check legal/illegal transitions; terminal immutability; approval invalidation; monotonic attempt/fence; no effect before admission/gate; every lease terminates/expires; every run reaches terminal or a named wait with owner/deadline.
fault: Crash before/after effect and receipt; duplicate/out-of-order/missing webhook; timeout with unknown effect; database failover; artifact corruption; worker partition; stale lease; compensation failure; external 429/5xx; replay from ledger; restore drill.
security_privacy: Tenant/repo isolation; confused-deputy and cross-repo token tests; path/egress allowlist; prompt-injection corpus; secret canaries; artifact ACL and deletion/legal-hold; consent/suppression race; audience-size explosion; unapproved publish/send/CRM mutation negative tests; audit tamper test.
evaluation: Engineering: representative accepted/failed/withdrawn tasks, exact-head acceptance, escaped defects, reviewer time, cost/cycle time versus baseline. Research: citation precision/recall, unsupported claims, conflicts missed. GTM: brand/legal/privacy defect rates, reviewer edits, deliverability/complaints, incrementality/qualified pipeline with holdout; not vendor-generated engagement alone.
acceptance_gates: Kernel shadow for >=30 engineering items; 100% duplicate-effect tests idempotent; zero unauthorized effect in adversarial suite; restore/replay and kill switch pass; all terminal outcomes accounted.
Engineering bounded write pilot >=50 attempts and >=30 days with predeclared quality/cost/reviewer thresholds before broader autonomy.

GTM starts only after shared-kernel extraction gate, separate repo/identity/data DPIA or equivalent review, system-of-record mappings, approval roles, suppression/consent tests and an accountable business owner. Draft-only pilot first; no send/publish/CRM write.

Each high-impact GTM trigger unlocks separately after shadow/dry-run and >=2 campaign cycles or a statistically/operationally adequate local sample; zero severe privacy/consent/brand violations; acceptable complaints/bounces; measured reviewer burden; credible holdout or causal design.

minimum_build: PostgreSQL event/command/outbox/lease/approval/receipt tables; object store for immutable artifacts; schema registry in Git; controller with fixed transition engine; scheduler; reconciler; short-lived capability broker; audit/metrics; CLI validate/plan/replay.
Fixed adapters only: OCI command, model inference, GitHub, HTTP allowlist, object store, Postgres and human approval.
Engineering domain schemas/policy in the existing repository; GitHub as intake/PR/check projection; controller ledger as live authority.
Research/writing factory as a non-production conformance fixture to pressure-test artifacts/fanout/citations.
explicitly_not_now: multi-agent society/role language in the kernel
Temporal/Kubernetes unless measured scale/recovery need justifies operations cost
stages: 0: document kernel ADR and implement engineering state/ledger without generic branding.
1: operate engineering end to end; collect missing-abstraction log.
2: extract only the nine stable nouns/interfaces; run research fixture against them.
3: if gates pass, create isolated GTM config repository; observe/draft only.
4: unlock one reversible GTM effect at a time; keep publication/send/consent/identity high-gated.
implementation_recommendation.extraction_gate: Extract a shared domain-kit only when engineering is stable, research fixture reuses >=80% of kernel without semantic special cases, at least three repeated cross-domain needs exist, no domain concept has leaked into kernel schemas, upgrade/isolation/replay tests pass, and two named domain owners accept the interface. Until then, copy a schema or add a narrow internal API rather than promise compatibility.
implementation_recommendation.value_gate: Fund GTM only with named owner, 2-3 costly repeatable workflows, measurable baseline/denominator, accessible governed data, explicit privacy/brand/channel approvals, plausible payback after reviewer/ops cost and stop criteria. Kill if draft acceptance, time/cost, compliance defects or causal business outcomes do not beat the baseline in the pilot.
implementation_recommendation.decision: Proceed with the small shared kernel as an internal implementation boundary, engineering first. Do not build a universal platform. Treat GTM as a separately secured customer of the kernel whose triggers are disabled until local evidence and governance gates pass.

sources.limitations: Does not include this proposal’s complete authority, provenance and protected-improvement policy.

sources.title: Multi-tenancy
sources.claims_used: Namespaces, RBAC, quotas, networking/storage isolation and harder isolation options.
sources.limitations: Namespaces are soft boundaries; actual isolation depends on cluster configuration and shared control plane/nodes.

sources.title: Secrets
sources.claims_used: Secrets need encryption/access restriction; Pod-creation authority can expose namespace secrets.
sources.limitations: Kubernetes-specific; external secret broker and workload identity still need threat testing.

sources.title: SPIFFE ID Specification
sources.claims_used: URI workload identities and trust-domain semantics support per-project role identities.
sources.limitations: Identity format does not define application authorization policy.

sources.title: OCI Distribution Specification
sources.claims_used: Content-agnostic digest-addressed artifact distribution and referrer/subject relations.
sources.limitations: Registry access control, retention and domain policy remain deployment-owned.

sources.title: Strategies for the Integration of Software Supply Chain Security in DevSecOps CI/CD Pipelines (SP 800-204D)
sources.author_or_maintainer: Ramaswamy Chandramouli, John Kautz, Santiago Torres-Arias
sources.source_type: government technical publication / independent control guidance
sources.claims_used: Granular authorization, verification as artifacts move between repositories, isolated builds and higher-trust evidence.
sources.limitations: Software supply-chain scope; GTM/research application is architectural inference.

sources.title: Approvals for campaigns and Canvases
sources.claims_used: Message, delivery, audience and conversion approvals; saved changes reset status; API/transactional paths have documented exceptions.
sources.limitations: Off by default; permitted self-approval and unsupported API paths mean UI workflow cannot be the final authority.

sources.title: Braze permissions
sources.claims_used: Separate view/edit/send/approval/settings permissions and workspace scope.
sources.limitations: Admins can change settings; tenant configuration must be audited.

sources.title: Publishing Pages from the Sites Console
sources.publisher: Adobe Experience Manager as a Cloud Service Documentation
sources.claims_used: Author/preview/publish/unpublish boundaries, privilege workflow and reference publication behavior.
sources.limitations: Quick Publish dependency behavior requires explicit publication-package closure and tenant tests.

sources.title: GenStudio for Performance Marketing Brands
sources.claims_used: Versioned brand guidelines/states can constrain generation and validation.
sources.limitations: “On-brand” is a vendor feature claim, not audited correctness or claim substantiation.

sources.title: Advertising and Marketing Basics
sources.claims_used: Material advertising claims must be truthful, nondeceptive and appropriately substantiated.
sources.limitations: General US guidance; specialized sectors and jurisdictions add rules.

sources.title: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)
sources.author_or_maintainer: California Office of the Attorney General
sources.publisher: State of California Department of Justice
sources.claims_used: Consumer access/delete/correct and sale/sharing opt-out/GPC boundaries for covered businesses.
sources.limitations: Applicability and detailed duties need counsel and current regulations.

sources.title: Attorney General Bonta Announces Settlement with Sephora
sources.author_or_maintainer: California Office of the Attorney General
sources.publisher: State of California Department of Justice
sources.claims_used: $1.2m settlement and alleged failures around sale disclosure, opt-out and GPC show real enforcement stakes.
sources.limitations: Single settlement/allegations, not a general rate of failure or legal advice.

sources.title: Generative AI at Work
sources.author_or_maintainer: Erik Brynjolfsson, Danielle Li, Lindsey R. Raymond
sources.publisher: NBER; later Quarterly Journal of Economics
sources.source_type: independent working paper / peer-reviewed field evidence
sources.claims_used: Staggered support-agent rollout found heterogeneous productivity gains; supports domain/task-specific measurement.
sources.limitations: Customer support, not marketing; not evidence of autonomous publication or attribution.

sources.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier
sources.claims_used: BCG consultant experiment found gains inside the model frontier and worse correctness outside it.
sources.limitations: Specific model/tasks/sample; supports task-specific gates, not exact factory outcomes.

sources.title: Set up email subscription types
sources.claims_used: Subscription/legal-basis and opt-in enforcement behavior is configuration dependent.
sources.limitations: HubSpot warns local law may be stricter; product configuration is not compliance certification.

sources.title: Understand opt-in consent for email
sources.claims_used: Lack of opt-out is not verifiable consent; consent state must be explicit.
sources.limitations: Vendor guidance and configuration details; jurisdiction-specific law controls.

sources.title: Manage data retention policy settings for inactive contacts
sources.claims_used: Inactive-contact deletion/restoration mechanics and analytics impact.
sources.limitations: Tenant/SKU behavior needs testing; retention choice requires legal/business ownership.

sources.title: Guide to Salesforce Record Approval Processes
sources.claims_used: Approval steps/roles/actions and record locking show a real CRM governance workflow.
sources.limitations: Admins/approvers retain powers; not an independent separation-of-duties proof.

sources.title: Email subscriptions
sources.claims_used: Subscription/preference/unsubscribe states are operational objects.
sources.limitations: Braze says documentation is informational, not legal advice.

sources.title: Rate limiting and frequency capping
sources.claims_used: Dispatch and contact-pressure controls.
sources.limitations: Attempt/user caps may not equal delivered messages; not a quality/outcome guarantee.

sources.title: Create multivariate and A/B tests
sources.claims_used: Randomized variants/control and conversion tracking as workflow capabilities.
sources.limitations: Instrumentation is not proof of causal lift without frozen design, denominators and statistical controls.

conflicts.conflict: “Repository-native” suggests Git can own everything, but active leases, event order, approvals and external CRM/Project/channel state are mutable and transactional.
conflicts.resolution: Git owns desired definitions/schemas/policy; the durable controller ledger owns live execution; each external field declares its system of record and is reconciled. Git commits never impersonate observed state.

conflicts.conflict: Temporal/Argo/Tekton offer workflow abstractions, but adopting one as the domain model couples semantics and operations.
conflicts.resolution: Keep an engine-neutral kernel contract. Implement Postgres first; add/translate to a durable engine only after measured timer/history/operator load. Standards are inputs, not mandates [S3-S6,S38].

conflicts.conflict: CloudEvents/in-toto/SLSA/C2PA look like universal contracts, but each covers only envelope or provenance.
conflicts.resolution: Use CloudEvents for transport context and in-toto-style attestations for claims; keep domain artifact schemas and semantic validators local. Never infer truth, approval or value from provenance [S7-S10,S19].

conflicts.conflict: A generic domain pack resembles a plugin platform.
conflicts.resolution: A v1 pack is data only: schemas, factory definitions, policy and fixtures interpreted by fixed code. No dynamic code loading, registry/marketplace or backwards-compatibility promise. Runtime adapters ship through central reviewed releases.

conflicts.conflict: Cross-domain reuse favors common nouns while GTM demands Customer/Campaign/Consent and engineering demands Commit/PR/Test.
conflicts.resolution: Share only execution envelopes. Domain nouns remain schemas owned by their repositories and cross only through explicit HandoffManifests. Do not create a universal Entity/Task/Document model.

conflicts.conflict: Vendor GTM “AI” and journey tools support generation/orchestration, but audited safe autonomous outcomes are missing.
conflicts.resolution: Treat docs as capability claims. Require local denominator-based pilots, independent approvals, causal/holdout measurement and compliance/brand metrics before any trigger is enabled [S20-S24,S29].

conflicts.conflict: Automation seeks speed, but publication, outreach, CRM identity/consent and self-improvement carry asymmetric harm.
conflicts.resolution: Separate draft, audience, content approval, CRM mutation and send/publish effects; protect consent/suppression and promotion controls; automation may tighten but not bypass gates [S17,S18,S25-S28].

conflicts.conflict: Agent collaboration appears flexible, while empirical work reports coordination failure.
conflicts.resolution: Agents are replaceable workers. Typed artifacts, deterministic joins, budgets and independent checks are authoritative; chat/consensus never is [S31].

conflicts.conflict: Writing experiments show productivity benefits while engineering evidence includes slowdown.
conflicts.resolution: Do not average unlike tasks. Establish per-domain baselines and gate investment on local outcome, reviewer-cost and risk measures [S30,S32].

uncertainties.unknown: Exact live capabilities, plan limits and APIs of Salesforce, HubSpot, Braze, Adobe and GitHub at deployment time.
uncertainties.impact: Adapters and gates may need revision.
uncertainties.mitigation: Run version/tenant feature probes and contract tests; keep source-system writes disabled until verified.

uncertainties.unknown: Whether JSON Schema alone suffices for cross-field constraints or CUE materially improves authoring without adding authority ambiguity.
uncertainties.mitigation: Prototype both against engineering plus research fixture; store only compiled canonical bundle.

uncertainties.unknown: Whether Postgres remains simpler than Temporal once long approvals/timers and replay volume grow.
uncertainties.mitigation: Instrument history length, waits, retry ambiguity, replay time and on-call burden; adopt engine only at a predefined threshold.

uncertainties.unknown: Whether GTM supplies three genuinely repeatable workflows with sufficient governed data and causal outcomes.
uncertainties.impact: GTM may never justify a domain pack.
uncertainties.mitigation: Require named workflow/value gate; allow research fixture to be the second domain test.

uncertainties.unknown: Calibrated risk/disagreement thresholds for each GTM channel, jurisdiction and brand.
uncertainties.impact: False approvals or excessive reviewer load.
uncertainties.mitigation: Start deterministic and draft-only; collect shadow data and let accountable local owners set thresholds.

uncertainties.unknown: Retention/residency and deletion behavior for derived artifacts across object store, model provider, CRM and analytics systems.
uncertainties.impact: Privacy/legal risk and inability to honor deletion/holds.
uncertainties.mitigation: Complete data map/DPIA or equivalent review and deletion/hold drills before contact-level GTM inputs.

uncertainties.unknown: Adequate sample sizes and non-inferiority margins for low-frequency severe failures.
uncertainties.impact: A zero-incident pilot can give false assurance.
uncertainties.mitigation: Use adversarial/fault tests, conservative exposure caps, longer monitoring and never infer zero risk from zero observed events.

uncertainties.unknown: No audited study directly compares this minimal kernel with agent/chat-centric or plugin architectures across all three domains.
uncertainties.impact: Architecture is evidence-informed inference, not proven universal optimum.
uncertainties.mitigation: Use reversible staged extraction and retain missing-abstraction/exception logs.

confidence.overall: moderate-high for the minimal kernel and protected boundaries; moderate for exact schema/API; low-to-moderate for GTM economic value before local pilot.

claim_level.artifact/event/gate/capability kernel: high—supported by multiple mature standards and prior validated engineering studies [S1-S18,S35-S38].
claim_level.agents/chats should not be canonical: high—follows durable state/authority needs and independent coordination/security evidence [S31,S34].
claim_level.engineering-first and no plugin platform: high as a risk-managed design decision; not an empirical universal law.
claim_level.GTM workflow boundaries: moderate-high for artifacts/compliance/approval needs [S20-S29]; product availability must be tenant-verified.
claim_level.GTM outcome uplift: low—vendor docs are not controlled outcome evidence and no local baseline exists.
claim_level.Postgres before Temporal: moderate—appropriate at stated initial scale, contingent on measured workload.

confidence.evidence_mix: 59 claim-linked sources, including open standards/open-source primary docs, vendor/product primary docs, government/legal primary sources, enforcement reports and independent or peer-reviewed challenge evidence. Prior repository studies add validated project-specific synthesis but are not counted as independent URLs.
